lifecycle.label: Companion dog state machine
lifecycle.description: A new dog starts in Following. throwBall() moves it to Fetching. In Fetching, tick() returns it to Following while it has energy left and moves it to Napping when no energy is left. In Napping, whistle() returns it to Following.
lifecycle.caption: Each rounded box is a state; each arrow is a transition labeled with its event and, in square brackets, a guard on the dog's data. Events that leave the state unchanged, such as whistle() in Fetching, are not drawn.
lifecycle.source:
@startuml
layout horizontal
state Following
state Fetching
state Napping
[*] --> Following
Following --> Fetching : throwBall()
Fetching --> Following : tick() [energy left]
Fetching --> Napping : tick() [no energy left]
Napping --> Following : whistle()
@enduml

roles.label: State pattern role diagram
roles.description: Context holds exactly one current State and offers request() and setState(next). State declares handle(context). ConcreteState implements State and calls setState(next) on the Context to make a transition.

solution.label: State solution structure
solution.description: Dog holds its energy and one current DogState, and forwards throwBall(), whistle(), and tick() to it. Following, Fetching, and Napping each implement DogState. Dog does not depend on the concrete state classes.
solution.caption: Dog plays Context; DogState plays State; Following, Fetching, and Napping play Concrete State. The Context depends only on the State interface.
solution.source:
@startuml
class Dog {
  + energy
  - state: DogState
  + throwBall()
  + whistle()
  + tick()
  + setState(next)
}
interface DogState {
  + throwBall(dog)
  + whistle(dog)
  + tick(dog)
}
class Following
class Fetching
class Napping
Dog --> "1" DogState : current
Following ..|> DogState
Fetching ..|> DogState
Napping ..|> DogState
@enduml

sequence.label: Sequence of the traced inputs
sequence.description: The game calls throwBall() on dog, and dog forwards it to the shared Following object, which calls setState(fetching) on dog. The game calls throwBall() again, and dog forwards it to the Fetching object, which changes nothing. The game calls tick(), and dog forwards it to the Fetching object, which calls setState(following) on dog.
sequence.caption: Each input goes to whichever state object is current. The messages appear as the narration reaches them; the panel below shows each reaction.
sequence.source:
@startuml
participant game
participant dog: Dog
participant following as : Following
participant fetching as : Fetching
steps:
game -> dog: throwBall()
activate dog
dog -> following: throwBall(dog)
activate following
following -> dog: setState(fetching)
activate dog
deactivate dog
deactivate following
deactivate dog
game -> dog: throwBall()
activate dog
dog -> fetching: throwBall(dog)
activate fetching
deactivate fetching
deactivate dog
game -> dog: tick()
activate dog
dog -> fetching: tick(dog)
activate fetching
fetching -> dog: setState(following)
activate dog
deactivate dog
deactivate fetching
deactivate dog

cards.title: Benefit: localized states
cards.text: Each state's reactions live in one class; a new state is one class plus its incoming transitions.

cards.title: Benefit: explicit transitions
cards.text: Each transition is a named call in the state it leaves; changing state swaps one reference.

cards.title: Liability: more classes, spread transitions
cards.text: States depend on their successors, and a new request must be added to every state.

cards.title: A good fit
cards.text: Several states with distinct behavior across several requests, and states that keep being added.

cards.title: Simpler alternatives
cards.text: A few stable states — extracted methods or exhaustive, checked switches. States that differ only in where they go next — a transition table.

cards.title: Not Strategy
cards.text: A client chooses a Strategy; State objects replace one another as events occur.

cards.title: Zoomies
cards.text: A whistle wakes a napping dog into the zoomies instead of a calm walk.

cards.title: Its reactions
cards.text: Tick races one lap, then follows. Throw starts fetching at once. Whistle is ignored.

cards.title: Your task
cards.text: Name the class you add and every existing line that changes.

cards.title: Context
cards.text: Several operations of one object depend on a state that changes at runtime, and new states keep arriving.

cards.title: Problem
cards.text: State checks scattered through every operation keep one state's rules apart and make every new state touch every method.

cards.title: Solution
cards.text: A Context delegates to its current State object; Concrete States implement one state each and choose the next state.

cards.title: Consequences
cards.text: Localized states and explicit transitions, at the cost of more classes, spread transitions, and costly new requests.
